items.title: Show HN: Use Claude Code to Query 600 GB Indexes over Hacker News, ArXiv, etc.
items.raw_content: Paste in my prompt to Claude Code with an embedded API key for accessing my public readonly SQL+vector database, and you have a state-of-the-art research tool over Hacker News, arXiv, LessWrong, and dozens of other high-quality public commons sites. Claude whips up the monster SQL queries that safely run on my machine, to answer your most nuanced questions. There's also an Alerts functionality, where you can just ask Claude to submit a SQL query as an alert, and you'll be emailed when the ultra nuanced criteria is met (and the output changes). Like I want to know when somebody posts about "estrogen" in a psychoactive context, or enough biology metaphors when talking about building infrastructure. Currently have embedded: posts: 1.4M / 4.6M comments: 15.6M / 38M That's with Voyage-3.5-lite. And you can do amazing compositional vector search, like search @FTX_crisis - (@guilt_tone - @guilt
items.title_zh: Show HN：用 Claude Code 查询 Hacker News、arXiv 等 600 GB 索引
items.summary: A Show HN project lets users query a public read-only SQL and vector database covering Hacker News, arXiv, LessWrong and other sites by prompting Claude Code, which writes SQL that runs locally. It includes email alerts for matching queries and currently embeds 1.4M of 4.6M posts and 15.6M of 38M comments using Voyage-3.5-lite.

items.title: You can make up HTML tags

items.title: A Koopman-Bayesian Framework for High-Fidelity, Perceptually Optimized Haptic Surgical Simulation
items.title_zh: Koopman-贝叶斯框架：高保真、感知优化的触觉手术模拟
items.summary: The authors combine a Koopman operator formulation of nonlinear tissue dynamics with a Bayesian calibration module based on Weber-Fechner and Stevens scaling laws, reporting 4.3 ms average rendering latency, under 2.8% force error, and a 20% improvement in perceptual discrimination for surgical simulation tasks.

items.title: EHRSummarizer: A Privacy-Aware, FHIR-Native Reference Architecture for Source-Grounded EHR Summarization
items.title_zh: EHRSummarizer：隐私友好的 FHIR 原生电子病历摘要参考架构
items.summary: EHRSummarizer is a privacy-aware, FHIR-native reference architecture that pulls targeted HL7 FHIR R4 resources, normalizes them into a clinical context package, and applies constrained summarization to produce source-grounded chart-review summaries; the authors describe prototype behavior and report no clinical outcomes or benchmark results.

items.title: HeurekaBench: A Benchmarking Framework for AI Co-scientist
items.title_zh: HeurekaBench：面向 AI 共同科学家的基准测试框架
items.summary: HeurekaBench builds benchmarks of exploratory, open-ended research questions grounded in scientific studies and their code repositories via a semi-automated LLM pipeline, instantiated as sc-HeurekaBench for single-cell biology; the authors report that adding a critic module improves ill-formed responses from open-source agents by up to 22%.

items.title: Length-Aware Adversarial Training for Variable-Length Trajectories: Digital Twins for Mall Shopper Paths
items.title_zh: 长度感知的变长轨迹对抗训练：商场顾客路径数字孪生
items.summary: The paper introduces length-aware sampling, which batches trajectories of similar length, and integrates it into a conditional trajectory GAN with time-alignment losses to better match distributions of derived statistics, with tests on mall shopper paths and public GPS, education, e-commerce, and movie sequence datasets.

items.title: Who is the Winning Algorithm? Rank Aggregation for Comparative Studies
items.title_zh: 谁是最佳算法？面向比较研究的排名聚合
items.summary: The paper proposes a framework that estimates each algorithm's probability of ranking first on a future, unseen dataset by exploiting complete rankings across a benchmark, not just win counts, and reports gains over existing methods in synthetic and real-world examples.
